title: The Pair Separator Ends the Syntax Pass
statement: Let $x$ be a binary string, $s$ a syntax-scanner state, and $i$ a natural number. Suppose $i+2\le |x|$, the bit of $x$ at position $i$ is $0$, and the bit at position $i+1$ is $1$. Starting from the verifier configuration on $x$ in the syntax state carrying $s$, with $i$ input bits consumed, empty work tape, and work head at $0$, after two steps it has consumed $i+2$ bits, with empty work tape and work head at $0$; its state is certificate-copy if $s$ is the exact-end state, and otherwise it is verdict with bit $1$.
replaced:
Let $x$ be an input with $i + 2 \le |x|$ whose bits at positions $i$ and $i+1$ are $0$
and $1$, and let $s$ be a formula-scanner state. Started in the syntax state carrying
$s$ with $i$ input bits consumed, empty work tape, head $0$, and empty output, after
exactly two steps the non-tautology verifier has consumed $i+2$ bits and is in the
certificate-copy state if $s$ is the exact-end state, and in the verdict state with
bit $1$ otherwise.
